campaign.name: Skoolit Katie Pilot
campaign.audience: Mothers managing school and activity logistics

videos.title: The school-email filter I actually needed
videos.hook: Your inbox should not be your family command center.
videos.script: Your inbox should not be your family command center. I use Skoolit to pull the dates, deadlines, and things I actually need to do out of school emails. Instead of rereading everything, I open one clear list and handle what matters. That is the whole point: less searching, more done.
videos.problem: Important dates and actions are buried inside ordinary school email.
videos.solution: Skoolit turns the useful parts into one clear list.
videos.cta: See what school life feels like when it is handled.
videos.caption: The inbox was never designed to run a family. Skoolit finds the dates, deadlines, and next steps hiding inside school email.
beats: Your inbox is not a family command center.

videos.title: I stopped using my brain as the reminder app
videos.hook: I used to read a school email and tell myself, I will remember that.
videos.script: I used to read a school email and tell myself, I will remember that. Which was adorable. By dinner, it was gone. Now Skoolit pulls out the date or action and keeps it where I can actually see it. I still make the decisions. I just stopped using my brain as the reminder app.
videos.problem: Katie mentally files school tasks for later and loses them.
videos.outcome: Katie keeps control without carrying every reminder.
videos.cta: Your brain has better things to do.
videos.caption: I’ll remember that later has betrayed every parent at least once. Dramatization.
beats: My brain was the reminder app.
Skoolit keeps the next step visible.
Your brain has better things to do.

videos.title: The practice time changed
videos.hook: Saturday practice moved from nine to eleven.
videos.script: Saturday practice moved from nine to eleven. The update was buried under fourteen reply-all messages, so I arrived at nine with a kid, a water bottle, and absolutely no practice. Skoolit catches schedule changes and puts the new time where I will see it. Because reply-all should not control my Saturday.
videos.problem: A practice change is buried in a reply-all thread.
videos.outcome: Katie arrives once, at the right time.
videos.caption: Fourteen replies. One changed practice time. Dramatization.
beats: Reply-all does not get my Saturday.

videos.title: A schedule change should change your schedule
videos.hook: A changed practice time should not become a memory test.
videos.script: A changed practice time should not become a memory test. Skoolit recognizes when a school or coach changes an event and brings the update forward. The new time can replace the old one, so your family calendar reflects reality. The email can stay in the inbox. The change does not.
videos.problem: Updated times remain trapped in email.
videos.cta: Let the change change the calendar.
videos.caption: A schedule change should change the schedule—not become another memory test.
beats: Let the change change the calendar.

videos.title: My Sunday reset got shorter
videos.hook: My Sunday reset used to mean searching every inbox for the week ahead.
videos.script: My Sunday reset used to mean searching every inbox for the week ahead. School, soccer, music, PTA—then comparing all of it to the calendar. With Skoolit, the important pieces are already organized for me. Sunday is a quick check now, not a family logistics investigation.
videos.problem: Katie reconstructs the week from scattered messages.
videos.outcome: Her weekly reset becomes quick and calm.
videos.caption: The Sunday reset should not require detective work. Dramatization.
beats: Then I compared everything to the calendar.

videos.title: The permission slip disappeared
videos.hook: I opened the field-trip email and thought, I will do that tonight.
videos.script: I opened the field-trip email and thought, I will do that tonight. Then tonight became tomorrow, the message disappeared below the fold, and the deadline disappeared with it. Skoolit pulls the action and due date into view, so later does not quietly become too late.
videos.problem: A permission slip gets postponed and buried.
videos.solution: Skoolit surfaces the action and due date.
videos.outcome: Later does not become too late.
videos.cta: Keep the deadline where you can see it.
videos.caption: Opened is not the same as handled. Dramatization.
beats: I’ll do the permission slip tonight.
Skoolit keeps the action in view.
Later does not become too late.

videos.title: Not every email deserves the same attention
videos.hook: A lunch menu and a permission deadline should not look equally important.
videos.script: A lunch menu and a permission deadline should not look equally important. Skoolit separates general information from the things that need action, then keeps uncertain details available for you to review. You get fewer false alarms and a much clearer answer to: what actually needs me today?
videos.problem: Everything in the inbox looks equally urgent.
videos.outcome: Katie sees what actually needs her today.
videos.cta: Give your attention a better filter.
videos.caption: Not every school email deserves the same level of attention.
beats: Lunch menu is not a permission deadline.
Give your attention a better filter.

videos.title: I did not want another parent app
videos.hook: Honestly, I did not want another parent app.
videos.script: Honestly, I did not want another parent app. I already had enough places to check. What I wanted was something that could read the school information I already receive and show me the part that matters. That is why Skoolit works for me. It removes checking instead of adding more.
videos.problem: Katie is tired of adding another destination.
videos.outcome: It removes checking instead of adding more.
videos.caption: Parents need fewer things to check. Dramatization.
beats: I did not want another parent app.

videos.title: The recital started thirty minutes earlier
videos.hook: The piano recital moved up thirty minutes.
videos.script: The piano recital moved up thirty minutes. That detail lived halfway down a monthly newsletter I never opened. We arrived while another child was already playing. Skoolit surfaces schedule changes instead of asking me to read every paragraph of every newsletter. My daughter gets an audience. I keep my blood pressure.
videos.problem: A recital change is hidden in a newsletter.
videos.solution: Skoolit brings the changed time forward.
videos.cta: Catch the change before the opening note.
videos.caption: The important sentence is often buried inside a newsletter. Dramatization.
beats: Catch it before the opening note.

videos.title: Both parents can work from the same plan
videos.hook: Family logistics break when one parent is the human forwarding system.
videos.script: Family logistics break when one parent is the human forwarding system. Skoolit gives both parents the same view of the kids’ schedule and action items, while keeping personal calendar details private. The family plan is shared. Nobody has to screenshot, forward, or ask, wait—what time is that again?
videos.problem: One parent becomes the forwarding system.
videos.solution: Skoolit gives both parents one family plan.
videos.outcome: The plan is shared without oversharing.
videos.cta: Share the plan, not the mental load.
videos.caption: The family schedule should not live in one parent’s head.
beats: One parent should not be the forwarding system.
Skoolit gives both parents the family plan.
Share the plan, not the mental load.

videos.title: I stopped being the household dispatcher
videos.hook: I used to forward every important email to my husband.
videos.script: I used to forward every important email to my husband, then text the important sentence, then remind him what the text was about. Very efficient system. Now we can work from the same family plan in Skoolit. I am still a mom. I am just no longer the household dispatcher.
videos.problem: Katie repeats information across email and text.
videos.solution: Both parents use the same family plan.
videos.outcome: Katie is no longer the household dispatcher.
videos.cta: Coordination should not be a second job.
videos.caption: Forward, text, remind, repeat. Dramatization.
beats: Then reminded him what the text was about.
Now we use the same family plan.

videos.title: The low lunch balance
videos.hook: The low-balance email arrived while I was buying groceries.
videos.script: The low-balance email arrived while I was buying groceries. I opened it, thought I would add money when my card was nearby, and forgot. The next message arrived while I was traveling. Skoolit keeps payments and deadlines visible until I handle them. Because opening an email is not the same as finishing the job.
videos.problem: A payment reminder arrives at the wrong moment.
videos.outcome: The task remains visible until Katie handles it.
videos.caption: The email arrived. The timing was terrible. Dramatization.
beats: I opened it. Then life happened.
